turns.t: Hello. Um. I've come for a review, and, um, I wanted to ask what I was supposed to bring. ~
Just yourself, that's fine. So what's been going on? ~
I've been getting wheezy, a lot more lately. Maybe three or four times a week, mostly when I go up the stairs at work.
Three or four times a week. How long has it been like that? ~
A while. A month? I can't remember. I wrote it somewhere. ~
That's fine. Does anything bring it on? ~
Stairs, cold air, the dog next door. I don't know. ~
How do you feel afterwards? ~
Out of puff, and then I'm okay. ~
And how's your sleep, does it wake you? ~
Not really. Sometimes. ~
I'd like you to do something for me. Keep a short diary for two weeks.
A diary? What do I put in it? ~
Each time you wheeze, write the time, what you were doing, and how long it lasted.
I'll try. I'll probably lose it. ~
Put it on your phone, in your notes. ~
Oh. That's easier. ~
Also, I'd like you to bring everything you use for it when you come back, so we can go through each item together.
Everything. Okay. ~
And think about whether anything at work could be setting it off, dust or cleaning products. ~
There's a new cleaner on the stairs, actually. ~
That's worth noting down. ~
I'll put it in the diary. ~
Do you have any questions about it? ~
I wanted to ask about running. Can I still? ~
Gentle exercise is good for you. Warm up slowly, and don't run in very cold air. ~
That's helpful. ~
Right. I'd like to see you again in four weeks, with the diary and all of your things.
Four weeks. Where do I write that? ~
The receptionist will give you a card. ~
Okay. I'll ask her. ~
Anything else for today? ~
No. I think that's all. ~
Good. Take care. ~
Thanks, doctor. Bye. ~
